key_insight: Long-lived orientational persistence combined with slow alignment can help self-aligning active crystals anneal defects and transform from polycrystals into single crystals.
engineering_relevance: Tuning activity-related timescales offers a potential route to autonomously reorganizing, low-defect materials without relying solely on thermal annealing.
method: Investigate defect-rich active Brownian crystals with coupled translational and rotational dynamics.
Separate activity magnitude from persistence and alignment timescales to identify annealing mechanisms.
Examine point-particle active crystals with delayed velocity relaxation toward polarized motion.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports poly-to-single-crystal transformations and similar defect annealing in point-particle active crystals, but provides no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: Experimental feasibility and the robustness of the required timescale tuning are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Tunable annealing of defects in self-aligning active crystals
